page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock frequency of 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include an extensive 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8). It incorporates 84.0 GB of system memory, yielding an unusually dense ratio of 42.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution driven by the high 4.2 GHz CPU clock speed. The instance achieved top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench (2342.0) and strong single-threaded throughput in compression workloads, registering 34.72 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.32 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, total throughput is strictly bounded by the 2-vCPU allocation, resulting in lower-tier multithreaded benchmarks such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 2884.0, PassMark CPU score of 4149.25, and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 2217.08. Memory bandwidth on uncached block operations also remains restricted, recording 21.11 GB/sec on large block reads and 14.3 GB/sec on writes.

The qualitative cost profile reflects a hardware footprint tailored toward software licensing models billed per core that simultaneously require substantial memory and fast individual core execution. Because compute resources are constrained to a single dual-threaded core, workloads requiring high aggregate parallel throughput will encounter severe bottlenecks. However, for operations constrained by memory footprint or single-thread performance, it offers high resource density per licensed core.

The FX4-2mds_v2 is suited for single-threaded or low-concurrency database instances, memory-bound caching layers, financial modeling algorithms, electronic design automation (EDA) tasks, and in-memory analytics requiring rapid per-core processing combined with local scratch space on high-speed NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is a compute and memory configuration featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Designed on x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, it includes 260 MB of L3 cache, support for AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions, 84.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD without GPU acceleration. The server delivers high single-threaded performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2342.0 and strong gzip compression speeds of 34.72 GB/sec. However, aggregate parallel throughput remains limited due to the dual-thread ceiling. This hardware profile provides high per-core memory density, making it suitable for memory-intensive, per-core-licensed databases, caching engines, and EDA workloads requiring fast individual clock execution.
